clue.text: Stand-offishness shown by a section of the army?

definitions.meaning: aloofness or emotional distance from others
a body of troops sent away from the main force on a separate task

explanation.surface: Is an aloof manner what you'd expect from one army unit?
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both cool aloofness and a detached military unit, two senses of being set apart.

clue.text: How to lie, to hide track and get away

parts.note: to dog someone is to track or trail them
to go is to leave or get away

explanation.surface: Advice for a fugitive: lie low, cover your trail and escape.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'lie doggo' is old slang for keeping still and hidden, so the whole phrase 'How to lie, to hide' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying doggo means lying quiet and concealed, playing dead until danger passes.

clue.text: Sans teeth, sans eyes, and so lacking in discernment

definitions.meaning: Shakespeare's 'seven ages' speech in As You Like It runs 'sans teeth, sans eyes, sans taste, sans everything', so the next item is being without taste
having poor judgement in matters of style

explanation.surface: An old person, toothless and blind, is also judged to have no good judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition works by completing Jaques's line from As You Like It: after 'sans teeth, sans eyes' comes 'sans taste', i.e. without taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without refined judgement in style is said to have no taste, the quality the Shakespeare line strips away next.

clue.text: P Jones's instruction to broking firm ?

definitions.text: P Jones's instruction to broking firm ?

parts.words: P Jones's instruction to broking firm
parts.note: in the Paul Jones, a ballroom mixer dance, dancers are called to swap who they dance with; read as an order to a stockbroking partnership, it tells the firm to replace its senior members

explanation.surface: A dance caller's command is reimagined as a memo sent to a stockbroking firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The Paul Jones is an old British party dance in which the caller periodically tells everyone to swap dancers; a broking firm is run by partners, giving the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Paul Jones dance the caller's cry makes everyone move on to a fresh dancing companion.

clue.text: Covered way to under ground system

definitions.text: Covered way to under ground system

parts.words: Covered way to under ground system
parts.note: reads like a tunnel or entrance to the Underground railway, but means a lidded opening giving access to sewers or drains below the street

explanation.surface: Sounds like a sheltered entrance to the London Tube.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under ground system' tempts you towards the London Underground railway; the system is in fact the drains, reached through a covered hole in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A street access shaft, closed by a lid, lets workers climb down into sewers and cable ducts.

clue.text: Not the true value of names

definitions.meaning: a face value as opposed to the real worth, as with a token sum
relating to names or nouns

explanation.surface: A remark that names alone do not reflect true worth.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both 'in name only', as with a token fee, and 'relating to nouns or names'.

clue.text: Look after the food!

definitions.meaning: to maintain or take care of
as in 'earn your ...', meaning board and lodging

explanation.surface: An instruction to mind the provisions.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain something is to keep it, and one's keep is the food and lodging one needs.

clue.text: Call out " All right " in time for nightfall

indicators.note: the word 'in' says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: eve is the evening, the time when night falls
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Someone shouts 'All right!' just as night comes on.
explanation.definitionFit: To summon up a memory or spirit is to call it out or call it forth.

clue.text: Urgent opening of shop for record editions

parts.note: pressing means urgent

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Customers queue urgently at a shop opening for new record releases.
explanation.definitionFit: A vinyl disc is stamped in a press, so each batch of copies made is a run of discs from the plant.

clue.text: "The Fighting Téméraire"? No, this work lacks design

definitions.text: "The Fighting Téméraire"? No, this work lacks design

parts.words: "The Fighting Téméraire"? No, this work lacks design
parts.note: Turner's famous ship painting might seem to be a picture of combat, but the clue rejects that and points to a style of abstract art made by dripping and flinging paint without a plan

explanation.surface: An art critic rejects Turner's ship painting in favour of something formless.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fighting Temeraire is Turner's painting of a warship; Jackson Pollock's drip style is called by a name that could describe a battle picture, but it is spontaneous and unplanned.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pollock-style method of splashing paint spontaneously onto canvas rather than following a design is known by this name.

clue.text: Fuel-pipe causes idle talk at sea

parts.note: gas is chatter or idle talk
the main is a poetic word for the open sea

explanation.surface: A pipeline is blamed for sailors' gossip at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal supply pipe carrying fuel gas under a street is named this.

clue.text: Vermin steal inside — a cause of disease

indicators.note: the word 'inside' puts one piece within the other

parts.note: mice are vermin
to rob is to steal

explanation.surface: Rodents stealing indoors spread illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ or bacterium is a tiny organism that can cause infection.

clue.text: Choked by excessive development

definitions.meaning: smothered, as a garden by weeds
grown too much, read as two words

explanation.surface: A garden smothered by too much growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden choked with weeds has had growth beyond what is wanted.

clue.text: Pieces of news are also to the point

parts.note: item is Latin for likewise or also, used in lists
S is south, a compass point

explanation.surface: News stories that are relevant as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the point' looks like a phrase meaning relevant; 'to' simply joins S, a compass point, after ITEM.
explanation.definitionFit: News stories in a paper or bulletin are called separate articles or entries.

clue.text: Glide swiftly on by oar

definitions.meaning: to move smoothly and fast
propelled by a long oar, a ... being a big oar used on barges

explanation.surface: A rower skims swiftly along by oar.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a fast smooth movement and a long oar used to row a heavy boat.

clue.text: Bearing tax-rise with indignation in Norway

parts.note: S is south, a compass bearing

indicators.note: in a down clue, a rise reads the word upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: VAT is value added tax
anger is indignation

explanation.surface: A Norwegian complains angrily about a tax increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tax-rise' looks like one idea, but 'rise' tells you to read VAT upwards in this down clue, giving TAV.
explanation.definitionFit: Stavanger is a port city on Norway's south-west coast, the hub of its oil industry.

clue.text: Duke who got Nell in trouble

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nobleman is accused of getting a girl into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Duke Ellington was the American jazz bandleader; 'Duke' looks like a title of nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Kennedy Ellington, the jazz composer and bandleader, was universally known by the nickname Duke.

clue.text: Such an engine is a handicap, of course

definitions.meaning: a type of internal combustion engine with a two-phase cycle, as in mopeds
on a golf course, a handicap of two shots

explanation.surface: An engine type is said to be a burden, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' looks like 'naturally' but points to a golf course, where a handicap is counted in strokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Small motorbike engines fire every second piston movement, and a golfer receiving a pair of shots has that handicap.

clue.text: Removes unrepresentative paintings

definitions.meaning: takes away or extracts
non-figurative works of art

explanation.surface: Someone takes down the modern art.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both 'takes out' as a verb and non-figurative artworks as a plural noun.

clue.text: Boat caught by Sibyl

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a sibyl was a prophetess of the ancient world, an oracle

explanation.surface: A boat is grabbed by a prophetess.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round wicker boat covered in hide, used in Wales and Ireland, is this craft.

clue.text: What a heart-throb!

parts.note: an exclamation about an attractive star, read literally as the beat of the heart itself, its contraction phase

explanation.surface: A fan swoons over a handsome film idol.
explanation.walkthrough: A heart-throb is a dreamy celebrity, but read literally it is a single throb of the heart, the contraction that pumps blood out.
explanation.definitionFit: The contraction of the heart muscle that pumps blood into the arteries is the medical term here.

clue.text: Purge corruption of sale ring

indicators.note: corruption spoils or distorts something, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: Dishonesty at a livestock auction must be cleaned out.
explanation.walkthrough: A sale ring is the arena at an auction mart where animals are sold.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter aloes was an old-fashioned laxative, so the word means a purgative drug.

clue.text: Stage where aircraft get protective covering?

definitions.meaning: the part of a theatre stage in front of the curtain
the paved area at an airport where planes park
a garment tied on to protect clothes

explanation.surface: A theatre stage where planes receive shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: The forestage of a theatre, the airport parking area and a kitchen pinafore all share this name.

clue.text: Rates in which there's no commission

definitions.meaning: grades or classifies
the ordinary soldiers, as opposed to commissioned officers

explanation.surface: A deal on rates with no broker's fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commission' looks like a sales fee; it is an officer's commission, which ordinary soldiers lack.
explanation.definitionFit: To grade is to rank, and 'the ranks' are the private soldiers who hold no officer's commission.

clue.text: Sound detective agent rents a room with no end of trouble

indicators.note: trouble stirs things up, so these letters are rearranged
with no end means the last letter of room is dropped

explanation.surface: A private eye lets a room and gets endless bother.
explanation.walkthrough: ROO (room without its last letter) joins RENTS and A, and the nine letters are rearranged. 'detective' looks like a private eye but describes a device that picks up sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A resonating device picks out and amplifies particular frequencies, so it acts to detect sound.

clue.text: Supporters making pauses in the bar

definitions.meaning: props or stands that hold something up
in music, silences written within a bar

explanation.surface: Drinkers' props, or breaks taken at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub, but here it is a bar of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Props are things something leans on, and musical silences are notated with the same word.

clue.text: Low-down schoolboy booked, characteristic of the class

parts.note: gen is slang for information, the low-down
Eric, or Little by Little is a Victorian school story whose hero is Eric

explanation.surface: A badly behaved pupil is reported, typical of his form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'booked' sounds like being punished; it means the schoolboy comes from a book, F. W. Farrar's moralising school novel Eric.
explanation.definitionFit: Something general to a whole group or type, rather than specific, is this.

clue.text: Threatening order in the States — nothing in it

indicators.note: in it means a letter goes inside everything built so far

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit
US is the United States
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A menacing decree issued in America, with nothing behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something portending trouble is menacing or sinister.

clue.text: Hurry film preview

definitions.meaning: to dash or go quickly
the first unedited prints of a day's filming

explanation.surface: A quick dash to see a film's trailer.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurry is to dash, and a day's raw film footage viewed before editing is called by this name.

clue.text: Become members of society which invests

parts.note: to be is to become or exist
leaguers are members of a league or association

explanation.surface: People join a society that puts money into ventures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invests' looks financial, but to invest a town is the old military sense of besieging it.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest a city is to surround it in siege, which is what besieging forces do.
